title: Prepare an outage communication playbook for educators
description: Give Zedu educators and cohort organisers clear, honest guidance when messages, files or a Buzz session are unavailable. Deliver one reusable editorial playbook: an initial incident notice, an update with next-check time, a resolved notice, a post-incident summary template, and a short educator-facing fallback checklist. Include a decision table for suspected vs confirmed incidents, verified vs unknown impact, approval roles and safe channels. All contacts, operational ownership, response targets and alternative tools require team confirmation; do not invent uptime guarantees, root causes, data-loss assurances, recovery estimates, monitoring or a live status page. Avoid disclosing private learner information or internal security details. Distinct from the trust/security page, ordinary support replies, release notes and low-bandwidth teaching guide: this work covers communication during a service incident. Done when one complete, practical Markdown pack and a tabletop walkthrough are delivered and reviewed. No public notices, messages, website edits or incident simulations against real users are performed.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Add a 'before anything breaks' prep checklist that uses Zedu's real Download and link controls
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
The existing approach writes the messages for during and after an incident. This approach covers the step before: what an educator can do in advance so a short outage doesn't stop a class. It uses only controls that exist, from the public zeduchat/zedu-fe code (checked 22 Oct 2026):
- Every file in Files has 'Download' (_components/file-management/actions.tsx line 62), so the week's key materials can be saved locally ahead of a live class.
- Buzz has 'Copy buzz link' (buzz-management/buzz-menu.tsx line 44), and messages have 'Copy link', so important links can be kept outside the app.
- Zedu runs on web, iOS, Android and desktop ('Download Zedu on iOS, Android, and desktop', zedu.chat/download), so a learner can try another app if one isn't loading. This needs team confirmation that it helps in a given incident.
Tasks, each finishable:
1. Prep checklist (content): a one-page 'before each live class' and 'start of each week' checklist (download this week's materials, agree one team-approved backup channel, share the session plan), with only confirmed controls and placeholders for the backup channel the team chooses.
2. Educator message (content): a short note educators can send their cohort in week one saying what to do if Zedu isn't loading, linked to the incident notices in the existing pack.
3. Check (research): confirm each control works on web and mobile, and mark any that don't.
No uptime promises, no invented alternatives, and nothing sent.

upvotes.reason: Preparing before an outage beats reacting during one, and anchoring the checklist to the Download and link controls that exist in the app today keeps it usable instead of aspirational.

The control it relies on exists: in zedu-fe, _components/file-management/actions.tsx line 62 is { label: "Download", ... onClick: onDownload } in the default file actions (checked 22 Oct 2026). A prep checklist built only on shipped controls is useful and honest.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Outage playbook with pre-written status lines per channel and an honest comms ladder
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Approach: a four-stage template (detected, confirmed, fixing, resolved) with pre-written messages for the in-app announcement, email, and public posts; a comms ladder that says what to publish at each stage and what to hold back until confirmed; tone rules; and a fill-in sheet for incident facts only. Why it fits: educators run live classes, so predictable, honest outage messages protect trust and reduce support load. Done: the four-stage template plus per-channel message bank and the comms ladder. Measured: support and marketing can send a first message within 15 minutes of an incident using the sheet; no message asserts a fix before it is confirmed.
